{{Short description|German mathematician and engineer (1904 - 1959)}}
'''Karl Adolf Hessenberg''' (September 8, 1904 &ndash; February 22, 1959) was a German [[mathematician]] and [[engineer]]. The [[Hessenberg matrix]] form is named after him.

==Education==
From 1925 to 1930 he studied [[electrical engineering]] at the Technische Hochschule Darmstadt (today [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]]) and graduated with a [[diploma]]. From 1931 to 1932 he was an assistant to [[Alwin Walther]] at the Technische Hochschule Darmstadt, afterwards he worked at the power station in [[Worms, Germany|Worms]], Germany. From 1936 he worked as an engineer at [[AEG (German company)|AEG]], first in Berlin and later in Frankfurt. In 1940 he received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from Alwin Walther at the Technische Hochschule in Darmstadt.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hessenberg.de/karl.html|title=Karl Hessenberg|website=www.hessenberg.de|access-date=2019-09-16}}</ref>

== Family ==

Hessenberg was also the brother of composer [[Kurt Hessenberg]], and the great-grandson of doctor and author [[Heinrich Hoffmann (author)|Heinrich Hoffmann]].

The [[Ordinal arithmetic#Natural operations|Hessenberg sum and product]] of ordinals are named after [[Gerhard Hessenberg]], another mathematician and near relative of Karl Hessenberg.

His father was Eduard Hessenberg, and his mother was Emma Kugler Hessenberg.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hessenberg.de/karl1.html|title=Karl Hessenberg|website=www.hessenberg.de|access-date=2018-07-12}}</ref>
